messages:
morgan: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-routing change I'm seeing an unexpected latency hump on short prefill requests (seq<=64). p50 jumped from 6ms -> 12ms, p95 from 28ms -> 60ms. Not wide regression but consistent across 2 clusters. anyone else see this?

sanjay: saw similar in canary. looks correlated with the new kernel affinity heuristics that prefer attention_opt_v1 on smaller sequences. could be bad for prefill because it prevents decode-contiguous batching.

anya: can you paste the profiler slice? quick grep for kernel names + queue wait should tell us if it's queueing or kernel poly overhead.

morgan: here's an example from the trace (trimmed):
```
timeline: 
  prefill_enqueue -> 3.2ms wait -> kernel: attention_opt_v1 (setup 1.9ms) -> exec 7.5ms
  decode_enqueue  -> 0.4ms wait -> kernel: fused_matmul_v2 (setup 0.3ms) -> exec 2.1ms
metrics: p50_prefill 12ms, p95_prefill 60ms, gpu_util 72%
```

sanjay: setup cost for attention_opt_v1 looks high. Could be kernel init/logic for small batch paths. Also KV cache warming is happening during prefill which increases memory touch and can raise setup.

perf-bot: autotune run 2025-11-18-03 flagged >15% p95 increase on short-prefill workloads after change-1328.

kevin: hypothesis: the routing change binds prefill lanes to the same affinity as decode to increase kernel reuse, but for short seqs we actually hurt batch formation because prefill batches are too small and get dispatched to a heavier setup path. We should try separating prefill and decode queues again and add a phase-aware token_budget tweak.

anya: agree. propose: 1) add explicit prefill queue with soft token_budget=48, 2) let routing pick attention_opt_v1 only if batch_tokens >= 256, 3) add KV-prefetch hint to prefill path so setup cost overlaps with enqueue.

morgan: sounds good. quick experiment idea: keep current routing but force prefill->fused_matmul_v2 for short seqs and measure p95. If better, we can change the threshold.

sanjay: I ran that locally. forced fused_matmul_v2 for prefill seq<=64 reduced p95 from 60ms -> 22ms and increased prefill batch size from 3->8 on the test hotspot. decode unaffected.

kevin: sweet. any side effects on GPU occupancy?
sanjay: occupancy slightly lower (69% -> 65%) but overall throughput improved due to less setup churn. cost per token down ~6%.

anya: notes for rollout: set canary to 5% traffic with metrics dashboard for p50/p95 prefill, token_batch_size, avg_kernel_setup_time. Also add circuit breaker to revert if p95 degrades >10% on any region.

morgan: I'll open a quick PR with the routing guard and prefill queue flag. patch will include a toggle `prefill_shortseq_force_fused=true` and new config `phase_token_budget.prefill=48`.

kevin: also add a perf eval job that runs the short-prefill harness overnight to catch regressions earlier. link it to PR.

sanjay: one more thought — KV-cache thrash could still bite when prefill and decode share the same heap. if we separate queues, make sure the KV warmup policy keeps a short LRU window for prefill keys so decode cold-starts don't evict hot prefill entries.

anya: good call. add `kv.lru_hint.prefill=0.25` in PR notes.

morgan: filing action items now. thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: action-created: PERF-1483 "prefill short-seq routing guard + phase queue" assigned to morgan

kevin: I'll watch the canary tomorrow morning and report results here.

morgan: closing the loop — PR up: https://git.local/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/1829 (contains traces and metric dashboard link).

kevin: saw canary baseline: p95 prefill on canary dropped to 24ms, looks stable for past 30m. will mark canary green in 2h unless regressions show.
